why: The SQL is given verbatim and the steps are mechanical (custom migration, prune snapshots, a text test, three doc lines), so no design choice is left. But it is a migration that deletes production rows, and every database the checks run on (PGlite, CI's Postgres) has no cron schema: the guarded block never executes before the release job runs it on production. A dropped quote, a changed dollar tag or a wrong schedule string would pass every check and only show up in the release job, or as a wrong job in cron.job.
harm_if_wrong: A mistyped block would fail CI's release job and hold that deploy, or schedule a prune with the wrong interval or text that deletes more of pg_cron's log than intended or never runs, and no check before production would catch it.
brief_problems: The text test only checks for a few substrings, so a file that differs from the given SQL in any other way (schedule time, WHERE clause, the TRUNCATE branch) still passes; a check that diffs the file against the brief's exact text would hold it.
